🚨 HEARTBREAKING: The NTSB just released new details on the Learjet that left AUSTIN for the Bahamas and crashed in Florida, killing all NINE people on board.

At 35,000 feet, the crew reported ice and moderate turbulence
hits.draft:
After any plane crash, the first 48 hours are full of guesses.

Here's how the facts actually come out: the NTSB gives on-scene briefings, a preliminary report usually lands in about 30 days, and the final cause often takes a year or more.

Pray for the nine families. Save the blame until the investigators finish.

hits.draft:

patterns: Election-eve volume dominated: 91 hits (~2.6M views, 6.1% likes) mention voting, the midterms or ballots, led by Trump's Lincoln Memorial '$5,000' promise (~321k at 4.0%) and 'FINAL WARNING' last message (~176k at 10.0%)

Breaking-disaster posts bought the most reach with the fewest likes: Gunther's NTSB Learjet crash update was the top post (~1.44M at 0.6%), rawsalerts' San Andreas quake swarm (~832k at 0.9%) and dinosaur blood-cell find (~549k at 1.5%); 10 crash/jet hits pulled ~2.0M at 1.2%
Media 'blue wave' mockery worked as reach: 8 CNN/blue-wave/tsunami hits drew ~942k at 2.4%, led by 'PANIC MODE' CNN tsunami clip (~519k)

Michigan stayed the top battleground story: 26 El-Sayed/Michigan hits (~1.15M at 5.3%), including the Michigan campus-attack takedown story (~226k at 5.7%) and the El-Sayed supporter interview (~158k)

Short values one-liners again won on love: 'Every girl deserves a locker room without a boy in it. VOTE RED!' (~140k at 16.0%), the 9/11 vs slavery post (~106k at 14.1%) and 'ONE NATION UNDER GOD' (~71k at 12.4%)
Ask-Grok questions kept underperforming on likes: 8 '@grok' posts drew ~341k at 0.9%; Iran/Hormuz items (9 hits, ~560k) ran 2.3%
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, two searches, ~50 posts) was thin and spammy: the biggest items were crypto 'decentralized AI' promos (BitTorrent ~43k, AINFT ~20k) and an IIT Ropar clip (~19k). The substantive threads were smaller: reports that Anthropic shared a draft frontier-AI bill with lawmakers, a claimed 'rogue AI model' touching Georgia voter data (WesternJournal, unverified), Raptive 'ads for agents', November model-release chatter, and OpenAI/Anthropic IPO talk. Takeaway: no big AI story broke through on Election Eve; AI-and-elections privacy is the angle with legs.
narrative_synthesis: Election-eve window (Mon ~11:07 ET to Tue ~11:13 ET): 241 hits and ~11.6M views from 252 originals. Breaking disasters led reach (NTSB Learjet ~1.44M, San Andreas swarm ~832k) but with sub-1% like rates, while midterm vote-push posts carried volume and short values one-liners earned the love. For Election Day, the creator playbook: calm 'how results really come in' explainers, verify-before-you-share on disaster news, and short sincere one-liners.
